title: Empirical capacity experiment notes — multi-tenant GPU mix and autoscale rules
body:
Context:
This doc captures the notes and empirical results from the Nov–Dec 2025 customer POC experiments (re: multi-tenant Dedicated pool sizing, autoscaling heuristics, and back-of-envelope GPU cost comparisons). The customer use case: a mid-market SaaS product running a mix of short chat requests (avg 150 tokens, ~95% of traffic) and episodic long-generation jobs (avg 1.2k tokens, 5% of traffic). Latency SLO: p95 <= 350ms for chat. Throughput target: 4k concurrent chat sessions during peak.

Key assumptions (we agreed with customer):
- Model family: open Llama-2 style medium-large (13B) quantized to 4-bit FFN/attention where supported; fallback path to 7B quantized variant for extremes.
- Traffic profile: 85% requests single-turn chat, 10% short multi-turn (prefix reuse), 5% long-batch generation.
- Average token generation per request: chat completions produce ~40 tokens on average at steady state.
- Target cost sensitivity: customer wants to minimize spend while meeting p95 SLAs; willing to accept small fraction of requests routed to higher-latency fallback during rare bursts.

Experiment matrix (what we ran):
1) GPU types: A100 40GB, H100 80GB, L40s 48GB (for cost parity), and a CPU-only control for baseline (very slow).
2) Pool configs: homogeneous pools (N x A100, N x H100) vs mixed pools (primarily A100 with a small pool of L40s for background long jobs).
3) Autoscale triggers: queue_length (tokens pending), running_utilization (vCPU/GPU util), p95_latency crossing 300ms, and a hybrid rule (queue + latency).
4) Batching policies: continuous batching window 5–25ms, batch size cap 64 tokens per request, dynamic kv-cache reuse for multi-turn.

Representative raw results (summaries from bench runs):
- A100 (40GB), single-tenant throughput: ~920 tokens/sec at batch window 10ms, p95 latency ~280ms for 150-token requests. Cost (on-cloud list): ~$3.10/hr per card effective (region-specific).
- H100 (80GB), throughput: ~1700 tokens/sec, p95 ~210ms. Cost: ~$7.80/hr per card (note: higher spot savings variability).
- L40s (48GB), throughput: ~860 tokens/sec, p95 ~300–360ms; cost: ~$2.70/hr per card. Good for cheaper long-job capacity but slightly worse latency for chat.
- CPU: impractical for customer SLOs, 8–12x slower than A100 for these model sizes.

Observations and interpretation:
- For their traffic mix, a mixed-pool strategy is attractive: use A100s as the primary chat-serving tier (meet p95), and use a small bank of L40s for long-batch jobs that are latency-tolerant and can be scheduled with lower priority. This reduced overall committed A100 count by ~20% in our sims.
- H100 delivers clear latency/throughput gains but cost per token is not linearly better given current pricing. H100 works well when strict latency headroom is required or when heavy concurrency demands justify fewer cards.
- Autoscaling by queue length + cooldown performed better than util-only rules in preventing latency spikes caused by sudden bursty arrivals. Utilization-only rules were too slow to react to short-lived but high-concurrency bursts.

Proposed sizing example (customer peak = 4k concurrent chat sessions):
- Primary chat pool: 8 x A100 40GB (serves ~7.3k concurrent short-chat-equivalent with our batching assumptions and KV-cache); keep min=4, max=12 (autoscale steps of +2 cards).
- Long-job pool: 2 x L40s (min=1, max=4), scheduled with lower priority and pre-warm windows to allow start-of-job latency ~1.2s acceptable.
- Fallback pool: 1 x 7B-quantized variant on a cheap GPU (or a small CPU-backed pool) to absorb extreme overloads (graceful degradation).

Autoscaling policy (recommended):
- Primary rule: scale out when queue_length_tokens > 25k OR p95_latency > 300ms for 120s window (scale by +2 cards).
- Scale-in rule: if queue_length_tokens < 8k AND p95_latency < 220ms for 600s window then scale in by -1 card (conservative scale-in to avoid oscillation).
- Cooldown: 180s after any successful scale action.
- Pre-warm strategy: use scheduled pre-warms (cron-like) for predictable daily peaks (+1 card 15 minutes before expected peak).
- Priority routing: mark long-job requests as SLO-low and route to long-job pool; only route to fallback pool when both primary and long-job pool queue depth > thresholds.

Cost estimates (monthly, 720 hours):
- Config A (8 A100 primary + 2 L40s, average usage 80% of primary, 30% of long-pool):
  - A100 cost: 8 cards * $3.10/hr * 720h * 0.8 = $11,347 (approx)
  - L40 cost: 2 cards * $2.70/hr * 720h * 0.3 = $1,166
  - Total infra GPU spend estimate: ~$12.5k/mo (excludes networking, storage, control-plane).
- Config B (6 H100 primary, high-headroom):
  - H100 cost: 6 * $7.80 * 720 * 0.7 = ~$23,618 (approx). More expensive but gives more headroom per card.
- Notes: committed reserved pricing or Dedicated contracts can materially change these numbers; we recommended presenting annual reserved options to the customer (we ran quick TCO numbers showing 20–35% savings at 1yr commit depending on vendor).

Operational considerations and runbooks (short bullets):
- Pre-deploy smoke tests: a synthetic chat workload that ramps from 10% to 120% of predicted peak over 10 minutes to validate autoscale triggers and eviction/fallback behavior.
- Canary rollout for new model quantization: start 1 replica (10% traffic) for 24h; track generation quality metrics (perplexity proxies + custom prompt evaluation set).
- Cost anomaly alerts: integrate token-rate x cost-per-token estimate with daily delta threshold (e.g., 30% day-over-day).
- Observability: dashboards for p50/p95/p99, queue depth, batch window distribution, per-model cache hit rate, and per-route cost.

Open questions / follow-ups: 
- Customer wants guidance on whether to pursue H100-only for a subsequent growth phase — we should run a scaled H100 bench with the exact customer prompts (dec 2025 workshop follow-up).
- Need to confirm preferred HW vendors/regions for discounted committed rates and to model network egress costs for embeddings-heavy jobs.
- Confirm long-job QoS: can the customer accept preemption for long jobs during extreme spikes? If yes, we can shrink long pool even further.

Next steps (action items):
- SE (Ravi) to schedule H100 scaled bench by 2026-03-05 using production prompt set (ticket JIRA-SOLENG-1247).
- Pricing lead (Marta) to produce 12/24-month reserved vs on-demand comparison and share by 2026-03-10.
- Infra (Kenji) to draft autoscale rule implementation PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1108) with the recommended cooldowns.
- SE to prepare customer-facing one-pager summarizing the recommended mixed-pool approach and cost projections (due 2026-03-12).

Rough notes from the workshop (verbatim/quick bullets):
- "Batch window tuning was surprisingly sensitive — pushing from 10ms -> 20ms cut cost per token by ~12% but increased p95 by ~40ms"
- "Cache warmup made multi-turn nearly free for recurring sessions — important for SaaS chat apps"
- "Customer is comfortable with 5–10% of traffic going to fallback if cost savings justified"

Appendix (bench knobs):
- Model configs: quantized 4-bit, kv-cache enabled, beam=1, sampling top-p 0.92
- Load generator: 50% new sessions, 50% continuing sessions, Poisson arrivals with lambda adjusted to target concurrency
- Batch window: experiment set {5ms,10ms,15ms,20ms,25ms}
- Metrics gathered: tokens/sec per GPU, p50/p95/p99, avg batch size, cache hit ratio, GPU memory headroom, scheduler queue length

If anything above needs more precision (raw logs, per-prompt perf), I can attach the benchmark CSVs and perf traces into the linked ticket.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc lean for the customer one-pager. Highlight 1–2 concrete configs and the expected monthly spend range.
